title: The k-weighted binomial row sum
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the sum over all integers k of k*C(n,k) equals n*2^(n-1).

formal.statement:
(define-hyperterm F (* k (gamma (+ n 1)) (/ 1 (gamma (+ k 1))) (/ 1 (gamma (+ (- n k) 1)))))
(define-hyperterm T (* n (^ 2 (- n 1))))
(assert (forall ((n Int)) (=> (>= n 1) (= (sum ((k Int)) F) T))))

evidence.supports: the creative-telescoping certificate, replayed by a checker that shares no code with the search that produced it
checkers: telescoping_check::confirm_ratios (shift ratios against exact bignum factorials)
telescoping_check::confirm_telescoping (pointwise identity and summed recurrence, exact bignum)
evidence.notes: Certificate: order 1, recurrence coefficients a_0 = 2n + 2, a_1 = -n (i.e. n*S(n+1) = (2n+2)*S(n)), R(n,k) = (k - 1)*(n + 1) / (n - k + 1). Closed form n*2^(n-1) verified to satisfy the same recurrence; base case S(1) = 1 = 1*2^0 checked by exact summation; leading coefficient -n has its only integer zero at n = 0, below the base, so the recurrence runs forward from n = 1. The vanishing at n = 0 is why the statement starts at 1.

provenance.established_by: lane telescoping: axeyum_cas::telescoping::zeilberger (untrusted search) + axeyum_cas::telescoping_check (independent checker)
provenance.source: classical binomial identity, stated by this lane as a HyperTerm specification

prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source

notes: Established on the `cas-certificate` route: an untrusted linear-algebra search (axeyum_cas::telescoping::zeilberger) produced the certificate, and axeyum_cas::telescoping_check verified it with its own shift-ratio derivation, its own fraction arithmetic, and a cross-check of both against exact bignum factorial evaluation of the summand. The checker rejects perturbed certificates -- see the tamper controls in the same test file (P+1, 2P, Q+k, a wrong recurrence constant, a degree bump in a_j, a zeroed recurrence, a certificate re-pointed at a different summand, a clipped summation window, and two wrong closed forms are all rejected).
